name: Uber
basis: Normalized non-GAAP; remove investment revaluations and unusual tax items
evidence: Q2 gross bookings were $58.0B, trips grew 18%, normalized EPS was $0.81 and trailing free cash flow exceeded $10B. GAAP EPS of $1.17 included investment gains.
thesis: The scarce asset is aggregated demand, payments, dispatch and local supply. AI can improve matching and support before autonomy is economically material. The strongest version of the thesis is that autonomous fleets need distribution; it is not that Uber must win vehicle manufacturing.
bridge: CY2027 gross bookings of about $285B × 3.2% normalized net-income conversion ÷ 2.03B diluted shares ≈ $4.50 EPS. This requires roughly 23% growth over the Q2 bookings run rate and a modest conversion improvement.
bearStory: Autonomous operators retain customers, insurance and driver costs rise, and delivery competition forces incentives; $2.60 EPS and a 16× multiple.
baseStory: Demand and cross-platform usage grow; dispatch, advertising and operating efficiency improve earnings without requiring a mass robotaxi rollout.
bullStory: Autonomous partnerships expand supply while Uber retains distribution economics; $5.60 EPS and 34× require strong booking growth and confidence in durable take rates.
catalysts: End-2026: Q3/Q4 booking growth, EPS conversion and autonomous-partner unit economics.
Mid-2027: evidence that autonomous markets add incremental profitable trips rather than subsidized volume.
End-2027: repeat usage, buybacks and normalized earnings establish whether the marketplace remains the customer interface.
failure: Two quarters of bookings growth below 12% with deteriorating normalized operating margin, or demonstrable loss of customer ownership to autonomous fleets.
risk: High disruption uncertainty. Premium rides are only one use case; this is not a pure luxury-consumer investment.
classification: Analyst modeled outcomes; observed reference price

name: Intuit
basis: Normalized GAAP-like earnings including recurring SBC
evidence: FY2026 revenue was $21.4B and GAAP EPS $16.46. FY2027 guidance is $23.28–23.51B revenue and $20.12–20.36 GAAP EPS. From FY2027, non-GAAP earnings include stock compensation.
thesis: Small businesses need their books reconciled, payroll paid and taxes filed. Intuit already owns the records, distribution and expert escalation path. Better agents can increase task completion and service revenue; a free generic assistant still needs accurate records and execution.
bridge: CY2027 revenue of about $25.0B × 24% normalized net margin ÷ 267M diluted shares ≈ $22.50 EPS. This is above FY2027 GAAP guidance because calendar 2027 includes part of FY2028; it is not a restatement of company guidance.
bearStory: Generic agents compress prices, small-business churn rises and live-service costs offset efficiency; $16 EPS at 14×.
baseStory: QuickBooks, payments, payroll and assisted tax filing sustain growth; agent features improve retention and expert productivity.
bullStory: Enterprise Suite and assisted services expand the customer wallet while agent productivity raises margins; $27 EPS at 30×.
catalysts: End-2026: FY2027 first-quarter growth and paid AI-service adoption.
Mid-2027: tax-season assisted-service economics, QuickBooks customer growth versus price increases, and churn.
End-2027: FY2028 outlook and evidence that agents expand revenue per business after support and inference costs.
failure: Online ecosystem growth falls below 12% for two quarters, retention weakens, or tax/credit customer acquisition becomes structurally more expensive.
risk: Tax policy, free filing, SMB failures, Mailchimp execution and credit-cycle exposure. A low multiple is insufficient if the customer relationship migrates elsewhere.
classification: Analyst modeled outcomes; observed reference price

name: GoDaddy
basis: Normalized GAAP-like diluted earnings
evidence: Q2 revenue grew 7%; Applications & Commerce grew 11%. Airo reached a $50M annualized bookings run rate. Management reaffirmed about $1.8B FY2026 FCF; June net debt was $2.7B.
thesis: The distribution advantage is millions of existing entrepreneurs who need an online identity, a working site, bookings and payments. AI lowers setup effort and may improve attach rates. The outcome worth buying is a functioning business presence, not generated website code.
bridge: CY2027 revenue of about $5.67B × 21% normalized net margin ÷ 119M diluted shares ≈ $10 EPS. This needs high-single-digit revenue growth and continued net share reduction, not explosive domain growth.
bearStory: AI-native builders and agent interfaces erode hosting and site-builder demand; $5.50 EPS at 11×.
baseStory: Airo converts existing distribution into paid commerce features while the renewal base funds disciplined repurchases.
bullStory: Agent identity and commerce APIs become meaningful paid products and higher-value attach grows; $12 EPS at 22×.
catalysts: End-2026: announced December 1 Investor Night; inspect paid Airo bookings and revised financial targets.
Mid-2027: renewal behavior of AI-acquired customers and Applications & Commerce growth.
End-2027: FCF per share after stock compensation, debt service and buybacks.
failure: Airo usage fails to convert into paid renewals, or bookings growth stays below 3% while customer count declines.
risk: The AI narrative is much smaller than the core business. Bookings run rate is not recognized recurring revenue; debt-financed repurchases can destroy value.
classification: Analyst modeled outcomes; observed reference price

name: Fabrinet
basis: Normalized adjusted diluted EPS; SBC remains a valuation limitation
evidence: Q4 FY2026 revenue was $1.316B, up 45%; GAAP EPS was $3.83 and adjusted EPS $4.10. FY2026 revenue rose 36% to about $4.6B.
thesis: Qualified manufacturing, optical alignment, yield and reliable delivery can capture value across competing module architectures. Fabrinet offers exposure to optical volume without requiring one laser or DSP design to dominate.
bridge: CY2027 revenue of about $6.62B × 12.5% adjusted net margin ÷ 36M diluted shares ≈ $23 EPS. Revenue is about 26% above the Q4 run rate; the margin assumption requires continued mix and execution gains.
bearStory: Customers digest inventory or move production in-house; $14 EPS at 17× reflects contract-manufacturing cyclicality.
baseStory: Higher optical volumes and qualified capacity support growth while manufacturing execution preserves margins.
bullStory: Multiple customers scale 1.6T and new production ramps faster; $29 EPS at 30×.
catalysts: End-2026: FY2027 guidance and order conversion into actual shipments.
Mid-2027: new capacity utilization, customer mix and 1.6T yields.
End-2027: sustained margin and cash conversion after growth investment.
failure: Two quarters of sequential optical weakness, materially lower utilization, or loss of a major customer program.
risk: Customer concentration, low switching volumes during qualification changes, Thailand operations and customer insourcing. Manufacturing revenue is not recurring software revenue.
classification: Analyst modeled outcomes; observed reference price

name: Reddit
basis: Normalized diluted EPS; recurring SBC retained in model economics
evidence: Q2 revenue was $805M, up 61%, with $762M advertising and $43M Other revenue. Diluted EPS was $1.25; fully diluted shares were about 207M.
thesis: Human discussion and intent can improve ad relevance, search and licensed model data. The larger current earnings engine is advertising; treating all revenue as an AI-data royalty would misprice the business.
bridge: CY2027 revenue of $5.0B × 32% normalized net margin ÷ 200M diluted shares = $8 EPS. This needs substantial growth from the Q2 $3.22B annual run rate and stable economics; it is the most execution-sensitive consumer model.
bearStory: AI answers reduce search referrals, commercial content harms engagement or advertisers slow; $3 EPS at 18×.
baseStory: Ad tools monetize international users and intent better while human content remains valuable.
bullStory: Ad relevance, international monetization and durable data access produce much higher earnings; $12 EPS at 42×.
catalysts: End-2026: ad revenue per user and logged-in engagement versus search-driven visits.
Mid-2027: international monetization and renewal terms on data agreements.
End-2027: per-share cash profitability after moderation, infrastructure and stock compensation.
failure: Sustained engagement or referral declines accompanied by ad revenue growth below 20%, or dilution materially exceeds buybacks.
risk: High traffic, platform, content-quality and regulatory risk. Its 1% portfolio weight is deliberately much smaller than its raw expected-value rank.
classification: Analyst modeled outcomes; observed reference price

name: Adobe
basis: Normalized GAAP-like diluted earnings, retaining recurring SBC
evidence: Q3 FY2026 revenue was $6.76B, up 13%; GAAP EPS was $4.62 versus $6.13 non-GAAP. Adobe reported AI-first ARR growth above 150% and $2.52B operating cash flow.
thesis: Creation gets cheaper, but enterprises still need editing, permissions, brand consistency, approvals and document workflows. Adobe's opportunity is to monetize finished, governed output and creative iteration. The risk is real: lower-end creation may migrate to simpler products.
bridge: CY2027 revenue of about $29.46B × 28% normalized net margin ÷ 375M diluted shares ≈ $22 EPS. This is roughly 9% above the latest quarterly revenue run rate, with buybacks assisting per-share growth.
bearStory: AI tools replace paid seats and credits fail to compensate; $14 EPS at 10× represents a structurally impaired franchise.
baseStory: Professional workflows retain customers; AI credits and document products offset pricing pressure with moderate growth.
bullStory: AI-generated content increases production volume and enterprise orchestration demand; $27 EPS at 24×.
catalysts: End-2026: FY2027 outlook, paid conversion and retention, rather than MAU growth alone.
Mid-2027: AI-credit gross profit and enterprise renewal economics.
End-2027: whether net new recurring revenue and cash profit per share grow together.
failure: Creative recurring-revenue growth falls below 5%, net retention deteriorates, or inference costs rise without paid conversion.
risk: Freemium usage is not monetization. Competition from Canva, model-native tools and platform bundling warrants the highest software bear probability in the model.
classification: Analyst modeled outcomes; observed reference price

name: Nvidia
basis: Normalized diluted EPS; avoid investment gains; FY2027 non-GAAP includes SBC
evidence: Q2 FY2027 revenue was $96.2B, data-center revenue $89.0B, and normalized non-GAAP EPS $2.22 versus GAAP $2.46. Q3 revenue guidance was $108B; Vera Rubin was already ramping.
thesis: The advantage combines compute, software, networking and deployment speed. Agents can increase useful inference work, but token growth alone is insufficient: customers must earn enough to keep buying hardware.
bridge: CY2027 revenue of about $595B × 48% normalized net margin ÷ 23.8B diluted shares ≈ $12 EPS. This requires about 38% growth from the Q3 guided revenue run rate, rather than a repeat of recent triple-digit growth.
bearStory: Capex digestion, custom accelerators and lower realized prices compress both profit and valuation; $6.50 EPS at 18×.
baseStory: Rubin deployment and inference demand grow, with some margin normalization and buybacks.
bullStory: Capacity converts into profitable agent and enterprise workloads with strong system economics; $16 EPS at 33×.
catalysts: End-2026: Rubin revenue conversion and customer cash-generation evidence.
Mid-2027: inference deployment economics, competitive accelerator adoption and supply execution.
End-2027: useful workload growth versus depreciation, financing obligations and next-platform transitions.
failure: Sequential data-center revenue declines for two quarters with falling gross margin, or major customers cut orders while useful utilization deteriorates.
risk: Customer concentration, export restrictions and financing feedback loops. The reported production ramp is already underway; a 2027 initial Rubin launch is not the catalyst.
classification: Analyst modeled outcomes; observed reference price

name: ServiceNow
basis: Adjusted diluted EPS excluding SBC; use lower valuation and track dilution
evidence: Q2 subscriptions rose 24.5% to $3.877B; cRPO grew 21%. ServiceNow AI exceeded $1B annual contract value. Management targeted SBC below 10% of revenue by 2029.
thesis: Agents need workflow permissions, system connections, approval trails and accountability. ServiceNow can become the governance and execution layer across departments, provided paid AI activity expands the wallet faster than seat counts shrink.
bridge: CY2027 revenue of about $19.69B × 32% adjusted net margin ÷ 1.05B diluted shares ≈ $6 EPS. This is an adjusted-earnings model, not GAAP owner earnings; the SBC gap remains material.
bearStory: Seat pressure and bundled platform agents impair growth; $3.50 adjusted EPS at 22×.
baseStory: AI contracts convert into deployed workflows and renewals while existing enterprise distribution lowers selling costs.
bullStory: Cross-department adoption and governance become standard budgets; $8 adjusted EPS at 45×.
catalysts: End-2026: cRPO quality, organic growth and AI ACV conversion.
Mid-2027: renewal cohorts, production deployments and sales efficiency.
End-2027: margin gains after cloud/inference expense and net dilution.
failure: Organic cRPO growth below 15% for two quarters, or AI adoption rises while paid renewals and margins weaken.
risk: ACV is not recognized revenue. Federal deal timing, acquisitions, Microsoft and Salesforce competition, and stock compensation can overstate the economics implied by adjusted EPS.
classification: Analyst modeled outcomes; observed reference price

name: Salesforce
basis: Normalized adjusted diluted EPS excluding investment gains and SBC
evidence: Q2 FY2027 revenue was $11.3B, including $456M from Informatica. Agentforce and Data 360 ARR approached $3.9B; Agentforce ARR exceeded $1.5B under an expanded definition.
thesis: Sales, service and customer records are natural agent inputs, and enterprise distribution reduces go-to-market friction. The test is whether paid agent work adds profit after lost seats, model expense and acquisitions.
bridge: CY2027 revenue of about $51.4B × 28% normalized adjusted net margin ÷ 900M diluted shares ≈ $16 EPS. Repurchases help, but the model removes investment gains and does not annualize Q2's unusual EPS.
bearStory: Seat erosion and acquisitions mask weak organic growth; $11 adjusted EPS at 14×.
baseStory: Data integration and paid service-agent usage allow modest organic reacceleration.
bullStory: Agent work expands the wallet and turns existing records into high-margin execution; $20 adjusted EPS at 28×.
catalysts: End-2026: organic cRPO and ARR definitions, acquisition integration and net buyback effect.
Mid-2027: paid usage, retention and service-cost savings.
End-2027: organic growth and profit after seat cannibalization establish a durable agent business.
failure: Organic subscription growth remains below 5% despite fast reported AI ARR growth, or FCF per share fails to improve after buybacks.
risk: Reported revenue includes acquired growth; agent ARR includes additional products. Neither a new name for existing revenue nor work-unit counts establish incremental demand.
classification: Analyst modeled outcomes; observed reference price

name: Toast
basis: Normalized GAAP-like diluted EPS
evidence: Q2 locations reached about 180k and ARR $2.4B. Recurring gross profit grew 31% on a GAAP basis; EPS was $0.26. Q2 FCF fell despite higher income.
thesis: Restaurants buy labor savings, repeat visits and less administrative work. Toast already sees the transaction and operating context needed for useful agents. Its primary opportunity is merchant software and payments, not unproven sales of restaurant records to labs.
bridge: CY2027 subscription-plus-fintech gross profit of about $2.95B × 32% net-income conversion ÷ 590M diluted shares ≈ $1.60 EPS. Gross-profit conversion is more useful here than a headline revenue multiple because payments include pass-through costs.
bearStory: Restaurant closures, weak same-store demand and payments competition hurt growth; $0.80 EPS at 18×.
baseStory: Location growth, useful paid AI features and operating leverage support earnings.
bullStory: AI improves merchant sales and retention enough to expand attach and margins; $2.20 EPS at 38×.
catalysts: End-2026: IQ paid adoption, net new locations and gross profit per location.
Mid-2027: merchant retention and measurable labor or marketing ROI.
End-2027: cash conversion, profitability and expansion beyond the original restaurant base.
failure: Location growth below 12% with declining recurring gross profit per location or rising merchant churn.
risk: SMB credit and failure rates, consumer trade-down, processor competition and working-capital timing. AI usage must translate into merchant value and paid renewals.
classification: Analyst modeled outcomes; observed reference price

name: Broadcom
basis: Normalized adjusted diluted EPS; cash generation and SBC checked separately
evidence: Q3 FY2026 revenue was $29.6B and AI semiconductor revenue $16.7B. GAAP EPS was $2.68 versus $3.32 adjusted; quarterly FCF was $13.7B. Q4 AI revenue guidance was $21.7B.
thesis: Custom accelerators and networking let hyperscalers optimize cost and power for predictable workloads. Broadcom can earn across accelerator silicon and the network, while infrastructure software supplies cash.
bridge: CY2027 revenue of about $189B × 45% adjusted net margin ÷ 5.0B diluted shares ≈ $17 EPS. This requires about 36% growth above the Q4 total-revenue guidance run rate and continued rich mix.
bearStory: Large programs slip, customers concentrate design value internally and margins normalize; $10 adjusted EPS at 18×.
baseStory: Custom programs ramp and Ethernet demand broadens, with software cash funding investment.
bullStory: Multiple large accelerator programs scale alongside networking; $23 adjusted EPS at 34×.
catalysts: End-2026: Q4 AI revenue conversion and FY2027 program outlook.
Mid-2027: execution across more than one hyperscaler and networking attach.
End-2027: custom-silicon gross profit, customer concentration and repeat orders.
failure: Program delays accompanied by declining AI revenue expectations or materially lower cash conversion.
risk: A few buyers have enormous negotiating power. Revenue from custom systems can have different margins; AI revenue growth cannot be valued independently of incremental profit.
classification: Analyst modeled outcomes; observed reference price

name: RELX ADR
basis: Adjusted EPS per NYSE ADR translated at assumed GBP/USD 1.30
evidence: First-half revenue was £4.871B with 7% underlying growth; adjusted EPS was 68.6p and cash conversion 98%. Risk and Legal showed growth in embedded analytics and tools.
thesis: Permissioned content, risk data and professional workflows are valuable when error costs matter. LexisNexis can sell ongoing decisions and task completion, not just text access. The US legal and insurance markets make this relevant to a US demand thesis.
bridge: CY2027 revenue of roughly £10.8B × 26.6% adjusted net margin ÷ 1.70B shares × assumed GBP/USD 1.30 ≈ $2.20 per ADR. FX is an explicit modeling assumption, not a quoted forward rate.
bearStory: Professional agents bypass incumbent interfaces or procurement pressures pricing; $1.50 per ADR at 18×.
baseStory: Paid legal and risk tools compound with modest margin expansion.
bullStory: AI workflows improve product value and accelerate recurring growth; $2.60 per ADR at 30×.
catalysts: End-2026: underlying Legal and Risk growth, with attention to print-related comparison changes.
Mid-2027: renewal prices, AI attach and scientific-research customer retention.
End-2027: profit growth and cash conversion demonstrate that content access retains value.
failure: Core Legal/Risk growth falls below 5% and customer retention weakens while AI development costs rise.
risk: GBP translation, publishing and institutional budget pressure, and competition from Thomson Reuters and model-native legal tools. Watchlist weight reflects overlap with TRI and other data businesses.
classification: Analyst modeled outcomes; observed reference price

name: TSMC ADR
basis: Normalized earnings per NYSE ADR in USD; five ordinary shares per ADR
evidence: Q3 revenue was $46.72B and diluted EPS $4.60 per ADR. Gross margin was 66.4%; 2nm represented 8% of wafer revenue. Q4 revenue guidance was $52.3–54.3B.
thesis: TSMC supplies competing GPU and custom-accelerator designers. That reduces the need to predict the winning chip architecture. Leading-edge manufacturing and packaging capacity remain difficult to replicate quickly.
bridge: CY2027 revenue of about $248B × 48% normalized net margin ÷ 5.18B ADR-equivalent diluted shares ≈ $23 EPS. This is roughly 16% above the Q4 guidance run rate; net margin is below Q3's 51.1%.
bearStory: Demand digestion and overseas-fab costs compress profit; $14 per ADR at 17×. A Taiwan conflict could be much worse than this operating bear case.
baseStory: 2nm, packaging and AI chip demand scale, with overseas costs partly offset by pricing and utilization.
bullStory: Capacity expansion and leading-edge demand maintain exceptional returns; $29 per ADR at 30×.
catalysts: End-2026: 2nm ramp, Q4 guidance delivery and packaging utilization.
Mid-2027: 2nm/A16 execution and incremental capacity conversion; timing depends on customer qualifications.
End-2027: revenue per wafer, overseas margins and capital returns validate the capacity investment.
failure: Leading-edge utilization deteriorates while capex stays high, or the technology/packaging execution advantage narrows materially.
risk: Taiwan concentration is shared across much of the portfolio. Foreign listing status does not provide geographic operating diversification for US fabless chip holdings.
classification: Analyst modeled outcomes; observed reference price

name: Microsoft
basis: Normalized diluted EPS excluding investment gains and unusual tax items
evidence: FY2026 revenue was $331.8B. Azure surpassed $100B annual revenue and Microsoft 365 Copilot exceeded 30M paid seats. Q4 reported EPS contained investment and other discrete benefits.
thesis: Existing enterprise procurement, identity and productivity workflows make Microsoft a natural agent distributor. Copilot, Azure and governance can monetize different parts of the stack; each must earn an adequate return on capital.
bridge: CY2027 revenue of about $396B × 43% normalized net margin ÷ 7.4B diluted shares ≈ $23 EPS. The scenario assumes growth plus operating leverage; it excludes mark-to-market investment gains.
bearStory: AI spending outruns paid adoption and cloud depreciation rises; $18 EPS at 22×.
baseStory: Azure capacity and paid productivity tools support durable growth despite ongoing investment.
bullStory: Agent adoption becomes a broader productivity budget and margins hold; $27 EPS at 36×.
catalysts: End-2026: Azure growth versus capacity, Copilot paid adoption and capex guidance.
Mid-2027: enterprise renewal cohorts, utilization and cloud gross margin.
End-2027: cash returns after leases and capex establish whether AI revenue is economically attractive.
failure: Copilot renewals disappoint while Azure growth and cloud margins both decelerate for two quarters.
risk: Large contracted backlog is not immediate cash profit. Frontier-lab concentration, open-model pricing, regulatory scrutiny and rising depreciation matter.
classification: Analyst modeled outcomes; observed reference price

name: Credo
basis: Normalized adjusted EPS with modeled dilution; large SBC gap remains
evidence: Q1 FY2027 revenue was $479M, up 115% year over year. GAAP EPS was $0.67 versus $1.20 adjusted, and Q2 revenue guidance was $525–535M.
thesis: Reliable short-reach copper links, optical DSPs and broader connectivity can coexist. The value proposition is delivered bandwidth, low power and fewer network interruptions; architecture changes create both new sockets and substitution risk.
bridge: CY2027 revenue of about $3.51B × 35% normalized adjusted net margin ÷ 205M diluted shares ≈ $6 EPS. This needs about 65% growth above the next-quarter revenue guidance run rate, making execution risk substantial.
bearStory: Customer concentration, socket losses or optical substitution compress earnings; $2.50 adjusted EPS at 22×.
baseStory: AEC demand persists while optical products expand the addressable mix.
bullStory: Several major customers scale the portfolio across copper and optical links; $9 adjusted EPS at 50×.
catalysts: End-2026: revenue guidance conversion and customer diversification.
Mid-2027: 224G/1.6T shipments and acquired optical-platform integration.
End-2027: profitable new sockets, cash conversion and dilution-adjusted EPS.
failure: A major design loss, sequential order weakness or persistent growth driven by a single buyer without diversification.
risk: A 40× base multiple still assumes durable growth. The gap between GAAP and adjusted earnings is economically significant; a copper-versus-CPO binary is an inadequate thesis.
classification: Analyst modeled outcomes; observed reference price

name: SK hynix
basis: Normalized K-IFRS-like EPS in KRW, excluding non-operating windfalls
evidence: Q2 revenue was ₩79.3T and operating margin 76%. Net profit exceeded revenue, so it must not be annualized as operating earnings. HBM4 mass shipments began in Q2.
thesis: HBM qualification, packaging and high-value memory mix create scarcity value, but conventional DRAM/NAND pricing still matters. Samsung's HBM4 progress is a direct competitive risk, not an automatic reason to assume perpetual shortages.
bridge: CY2027 revenue of about ₩400T × 36.5% normalized net margin ÷ 730M shares = ₩200k EPS. This deliberately normalizes profitability far below the latest quarter and strips non-operating windfalls.
bearStory: Memory prices reverse, supply catches up and KRW weakens 10%; ₩60k EPS at 6×.
baseStory: HBM and server mix retain above-cycle returns while conventional pricing moderates.
bullStory: Scarcity and HBM execution persist; ₩300k EPS at 11× with 5% KRW appreciation.
catalysts: End-2026: HBM4 shipments, customer agreements and underlying operating cash flow.
Mid-2027: HBM4E qualification and yield, pricing and competitor supply.
End-2027: normalized profit and capex discipline after capacity additions.
failure: HBM qualification/share losses plus falling conventional-memory prices, or contract visibility fails to convert into cash.
risk: KRX access and KRW exposure are required. No OTC substitute or ADR liquidity is assumed. Zero allocation in the US implementation portfolio; US investors already hold overlapping memory exposure through MU.
classification: Analyst modeled outcomes; observed reference price

name: Verisk
basis: Adjusted diluted EPS; cash conversion checked separately
evidence: Q2 organic constant-currency revenue grew 5.8%, with 8% underlying subscription growth. Adjusted EPS was $1.98; FCF was $298M, benefiting partly from payment timing.
thesis: Insurance decisions need standardized loss, repair, underwriting and claims data. AI can improve those decisions when embedded into existing processes. A model alone cannot cheaply reproduce validated industry data and acceptance.
bridge: CY2027 revenue of about $3.46B × 33% adjusted net margin ÷ 127M diluted shares ≈ $9 EPS. This requires high-single-digit revenue growth and moderate per-share leverage.
bearStory: Insurers internalize workflows and pricing power weakens; $6.50 adjusted EPS at 20×.
baseStory: Subscriptions and useful claims/underwriting tools compound with modest margin gains.
bullStory: AI tools meaningfully expand customer spending; $10.50 EPS at 33×.
catalysts: End-2026: subscription growth and recovery toward management's operating targets.
Mid-2027: customer renewals and paid AI-workflow adoption.
End-2027: FCF growth after tax/vendor timing and acquisition effects.
failure: Underlying subscription growth falls below 5% while retention or margins weaken.
risk: Data regulation, insurer consolidation and slow industry procurement. This is a durable-data thesis with limited disclosed stand-alone generative-AI revenue; watchlist status avoids duplicating TRI/RELX exposure.
classification: Analyst modeled outcomes; observed reference price

name: Thomson Reuters
basis: Adjusted diluted EPS; amortization and other exclusions require cash checks
evidence: Q2 organic revenue grew 8%, with 10% growth in the Big 3 professional segments. Adjusted EPS was $0.99 and first-half adjusted EPS $2.22; Westlaw and CoCounsel contributed to growth.
thesis: Professionals pay for trustworthy answers embedded in legal and tax work. Proprietary content, citations, workflow integration and institutional procurement provide a stronger monetization path than undifferentiated data resale.
bridge: CY2027 revenue of about $9.2B × 26.2% adjusted net margin ÷ 430M diluted shares ≈ $5.60 EPS. Growth and margin expansion must both contribute; the model does not annualize a seasonally weak quarter.
bearStory: Legal AI competitors compress pricing and professional seat counts; $4 adjusted EPS at 15×.
baseStory: CoCounsel attaches to the existing base while content and workflow improve retention and pricing.
bullStory: Agent workflows materially expand professional spending and margins; $7 EPS at 30×.
catalysts: End-2026: recurring organic growth and CoCounsel monetization.
Mid-2027: tax-season contribution, legal renewals and incremental AI gross profit.
End-2027: content-powered agents support pricing and earnings after implementation costs.

risk: The investment depends on trusted workflow economics, not merely owning text. Harvey and other private entrants can own the interface; model vendors can bundle research.
classification: Analyst modeled outcomes; observed reference price

name: Micron
basis: Normalized GAAP-like diluted EPS; cycle-adjusted rather than peak annualization
evidence: Q4 FY2026 revenue was $54.23B and GAAP EPS $32.87, with 86.8% gross margin. Q1 FY2027 GAAP EPS guidance was $37.84 ± $1.00.
thesis: Agent workloads need HBM, server memory and persistent storage, but the stock's outcome depends on price discipline and normalized profitability. A low P/E measured against scarcity earnings can be a trap.
bridge: CY2027 revenue of about $253B × 50% normalized net margin ÷ 1.15B diluted shares ≈ $110 EPS. The model is below annualized Q1 guided EPS of about $151; even the base assumes unusually high memory margins.
bearStory: ASP compression and capacity growth overwhelm bit demand; $40 EPS at 7× produces a severe drawdown.
baseStory: HBM/server mix and contracts preserve elevated returns while margins normalize.
bullStory: Scarcity lasts and capacity execution is strong; $165 EPS at 14×. This case needs pricing and cash collection, not only shipment growth.
catalysts: End-2026: contracted pricing, HBM allocation and Q1 guidance delivery.
Mid-2027: HBM4E production, competitor yields and DRAM/NAND price trends.
End-2027: through-cycle FCF after capex, inventories and customer receivables.
failure: Two sequential price/margin deteriorations with rising inventories or receivables, especially if capex remains aggressive.
risk: 35% operating bear probability and only 2% allocation reflect cycle exposure. The report does not infer future returns from the previous memory rally.
classification: Analyst modeled outcomes; observed reference price

name: Meta Platforms

bearStory: Ad spending slows while infrastructure costs remain fixed; $24 EPS at 17×.
baseStory: Core ads keep growing and operating leverage offsets some depreciation and AI development costs.
bullStory: Ad efficiency, messaging and new paid business tools deliver strong profit growth; $50 EPS at 30×.
catalysts: End-2026: ad pricing/volume and capital-budget discipline.
Mid-2027: business-agent monetization and expense conversion after infrastructure deployment.
End-2027: FCF after capex and leases supports the earnings recovery.
failure: Ad growth falls below 10% with persistent capex escalation and deteriorating cash conversion.
risk: The same equity wealth effect supporting premium consumption also supports ad budgets; it can reverse. Privacy, regulation, content quality and founder capital allocation remain material.
classification: Analyst modeled outcomes; observed reference price

name: Vertiv
basis: Adjusted diluted EPS
evidence: Q2 revenue grew 24% to $3.274B; adjusted EPS was $1.52 and adjusted operating margin 22.6%. FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance was $6.65–6.75.
thesis: Dense AI racks need power conversion, cooling and commissioning. These remain necessary across competing compute architectures. Service capability and installed-base support can outlast individual chip cycles.
bridge: CY2027 revenue of about $17.94B × 20% adjusted net margin ÷ 390M diluted shares ≈ $9.20 EPS. This is about 28% above FY2026 guided revenue and requires further margin improvement.
bearStory: Projects are postponed or orders were double-counted; $5 adjusted EPS at 19×.
baseStory: Power/cooling deployment and services convert demand into revenue with sound execution.
bullStory: Liquid cooling and broader infrastructure integration maintain rapid growth; $12 EPS at 38×.
catalysts: End-2026: announced October 28 earnings; organic orders and cash conversion.
Mid-2027: liquid-cooling capacity, project acceptance and service attach.
End-2027: backlog converts at the expected margin after working-capital and capacity costs.
failure: Order conversion deteriorates, cancellations rise or inventory absorbs cash while growth slows.
risk: Projects depend on power availability, permits, financing and customer execution. Backlog is neither cash nor guaranteed capacity utilization.

name: Coherent
basis: Normalized adjusted diluted EPS; net margin includes financing costs
evidence: Q4 FY2026 revenue was $2.05B, up 34%; GAAP EPS was $1.19 and adjusted EPS $1.74. Adjusted gross margin was 40.2%.
thesis: Lasers, materials and optical components can earn in several architectures, including pluggables and more integrated optical systems. The investment requires qualified production volume and yield, not simply a compelling bandwidth forecast.
bridge: CY2027 revenue of about $11.9B × 15% adjusted net margin ÷ 170M diluted shares ≈ $10.50 EPS. That requires about 45% growth above the latest quarterly run rate; the model carries a 35% bear probability.
bearStory: Yields disappoint, customer pricing tightens or optical demand is delayed; $5 adjusted EPS at 20×.
baseStory: Capacity and richer datacenter mix drive growth, with measured margin improvement.
bullStory: Optical engines, lasers and high-speed modules ramp across customers; $15 EPS at 38×.
catalysts: End-2026: fiscal guidance, datacenter mix and capacity deployment.
Mid-2027: 1.6T/customer qualifications and optical-component yields.
End-2027: cash generation after capex, debt and preferred/convertible obligations.
failure: Datacenter demand grows but gross margin and cash conversion fail to improve, or leverage/dilution offsets operating gains.
risk: Financing structure, industrial/telecom cyclicality, customer concentration and architecture substitution. Some CPO value can accrue to laser suppliers while module value migrates elsewhere.
classification: Analyst modeled outcomes; observed reference price

name: Amazon
basis: Normalized diluted EPS excluding investment mark-to-market gains
evidence: Q2 AWS revenue grew 37% to $42.2B and AWS operating income reached $16.6B. TTM FCF was negative $7.6B. Q2 net income included $53.4B pretax investment-related gains.
thesis: AWS supplies enterprise AI and model infrastructure, while retail, advertising and logistics bring established demand and data. AI can improve profit through operational efficiency as well as cloud revenue. It is a diversified economic capture case.
bridge: CY2027 revenue of about $1.0T × 10.8% normalized net margin ÷ 10.8B diluted shares = $10 EPS. Investment revaluations are excluded; retail and cloud margins must improve enough to support this profit level.
bearStory: Cloud capex remains heavy while retail demand and AWS returns disappoint; $6 EPS at 22×.
baseStory: AWS and advertising growth, plus logistics efficiency, support normalized profit growth.
bullStory: Custom chips, enterprise agents and retail efficiency produce sustained operating leverage; $13 EPS at 39×.
catalysts: End-2026: AWS growth, power/capacity availability and cash capex.
Mid-2027: Trainium utilization, paid AI workloads and retail fulfillment economics.
End-2027: FCF after capex and leases confirms whether AI investment earns its cost.
failure: AWS growth drops below 20% while capex stays high, or non-cloud operating leverage reverses.
risk: Reported GAAP EPS is distorted by investment gains. Negative current FCF and substantial reinvestment prevent treating accounting earnings as distributable cash.
classification: Analyst modeled outcomes; observed reference price

name: Eaton
basis: Normalized adjusted diluted EPS, including prospective portfolio changes
evidence: Electrical-sector backlog grew 43%; Electrical Americas organic sales rose 18%. FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance was $13.40–13.60. The Mobility separation was expected to close in Q1 2027.
thesis: Power delivery, protection and electrical equipment are necessary before AI racks generate revenue. Eaton provides broader industrial exposure and a concrete portfolio catalyst, with less dependence on a single chip design.
bridge: CY2027 continuing-business revenue of about $32.6B × 20% adjusted net margin ÷ 395M diluted shares ≈ $16.50 EPS. This assumes favorable mix and execution after portfolio changes, not a mechanically comparable reported-revenue growth rate.
bearStory: Project delays and pricing pressure offset backlog; $12 adjusted EPS at 22×.
baseStory: Electrical demand and mix improvement support growth while the separation simplifies the business.
bullStory: Capacity and operating leverage accelerate; $20 EPS at 35×.
catalysts: End-2026: electrical orders, backlog quality and capacity costs.
Mid-2027: announced Q1 Mobility transaction timetable and initial continuing-company guidance.
End-2027: electrical margin, delivery times and FCF validate the new mix.
failure: Backlog growth fails to convert, margins deteriorate or separation economics dilute per-share value.
risk: At about 29× FY2026 guided adjusted EPS, quality is already priced. Any spin/transaction consideration must be included in total-return accounting; the simplified price model is less reliable around closing.
classification: Analyst modeled outcomes; observed reference price

name: Alphabet
basis: Normalized diluted EPS excluding equity-security revaluations
evidence: Q2 revenue was $119.8B; Cloud grew 82% to $24.8B and Search grew 17%. Other income included a $98B net gain; reported EPS of $9.11 is not a recurring earnings run rate.
thesis: Search distribution, commercial intent, cloud and custom silicon allow monetization at several layers. However, agents can change search economics, and strong reported growth does not make the stock cheap at every entry price.
bridge: CY2027 revenue of about $625B × 28.8% normalized net margin ÷ 11.6B diluted shares ≈ $15.50 EPS. This requires strong Cloud growth and resilient Search economics, excluding equity gains.
bearStory: AI answers weaken ad economics while capex and depreciation rise; $10 EPS at 17×.
baseStory: Cloud growth and commercial AI search offset rising inference costs.
bullStory: AI improves queries, conversion and cloud margins with little search cannibalization; $20 EPS at 34×.
catalysts: End-2026: AI-search monetization, Cloud margin and capex.
Mid-2027: agent-mediated commercial queries and enterprise renewals.
End-2027: normalized cash profit after infrastructure spending and legal remedies.
failure: Search revenue growth below 5% with rising cost per query, or Cloud growth fails to compensate for weaker search economics.
risk: Antitrust remedies, distribution payments, inference expense and investment-gain distortion. Lowest modeled EV among the selected 25; the allocation reflects franchise quality and diversification across AI monetization paths.
classification: Analyst modeled outcomes; observed reference price
